newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ALPINE SKIING-DOWNHILLER ALPHAND TRIUMPHS IN SUPER-G.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-DOWNHILLER ALPHAND TRIUMPHS IN SUPER-G.

text.p: Luc Alphand, already one of the favourites for the world championship downhill, pencilled himself in as the man to beat in the super-G as well after claiming his first World Cup win in the event on Wednesday.

The reigning World Cup downhill champion blitzed down the sunbathed 2,266-metre course in a time of one minute 25.23 seconds to record his fourth win of the season and jump to the top of the overall standings.
It was the 31-year-old Frenchman's 10th World Cup career victory, his nine previous wins all coming in the downhill.
While Alphand's super-G victory was his first in 12 seasons on the World Cup it was not totally unexpected as he finished second in the final two events of last season.
"Last year I was so close twice, so I was confident today," said Alphand, who suffered a bad crash in Laax the last time the resort hosted a super-G in 1989.
"But I still think my best chance for a medal at the world championships is in the downhill.
"I think I'm more consistent in the downhill. But I will try my best in super-G because it's a second chance at a medal for me."
The race was the last men's speed event before the world championships in Sestriere, Italy, where the men's super-G will open the action on Monday.
Josef Strobl, who set the fastest time on the upper part of the course but lost out with a mistake lower down, settled for second place, crossing the line 0.12 seconds behind Alphand in 1:25.35.
But Strobl guaranteed himself one of the four Austrian places on the world championship super-G squad with his result.

"I really had to go for it today because I had not qualified in this event," said Strobl. "I have qualified for the downhill but I needed a good result here because we have so many good skiers in this discipline.
"Now that I have a place I just want to relax. The last three weeks have been very difficult."

Third place went to Italy's Peter Runggaldier in 1:25.63 while Norway's Atle Skaardal, winner of the super-G World Cup and world championship titles last year, prepared for the defence of his crown with a fourth place finish in 1:25.65.
The tough World Cup schedule has left the skiers little time to prepare for races.
"It's a problem for us, we had no time to prepare for this event," complained Alphand. "We raced in Kitzbuehel then we come here and train and then race.
"Now we have only four days before the championships and you cannot prepare."
With the win, Alphand now occupies top spot in the overall and super-G World Cup standings as well as the downhill.
The Frenchman leads the overall standings with 737 points, 20 clear of Norway's Kjetil Andre Aamodt, the 1994 overall champion and 1992 Olympic super-G gold medallist.
With four super-G races still ahead, Alphand leads the discipline rankings with 132 points, 21 points ahead of Austria's Hans Knauss who won the previous super-G in Val d'Isere in December.
